text:
alex: heads up — after yesterday's fractional consolidation rollout in eu-west we started seeing 95th/99th tail spikes on inference lanes for some tenants. small but persistent, started ~22:10 UTC.
maria: saw it on our dashboards too. NIC tx-queue depth jumped around the same time.
kevin: any obvious noisy tenant?
alex: not a single tenant; looks like consolidation increased cross-tenant egress coupling. p95 up ~40ms p99 up ~120ms on some racks.
kevin: can you paste the quick trace?
alex: here — sample from the proxy tail: ```json
{"ts":"2026-03-20T22:12:03Z","svc":"inference-proxy","rack":"eu-west-3","queue_ms":86,"egress_bytes":74512,"tenant":"t-42"}```
sara: deploy-bot shows a few preemptible compactions at 22:08, maybe coincident.
deploy-bot: auto-compact-run triggered by policy fractional-consolidate-v2 (run id: rc-20260320-19) :gear:
ops-lead: if compaction changed slot packing we could have shifted egress paths onto the same ToR, causing microbursts.
maria: agree. NIC head-of-line plus burst coalescing on ToR = spiky tail. we should avoid heavy cross-tenant egress on same ToR where possible.
kevin: quick mitigation: roll back fractional consolidation for eu-west hot-shelf and route affected tenants to reserved egress paths until we investigate?
alex: rollback is heavy. alternate idea: soft 'egress path stitch' — temporarily create an alternate SNAT set via the spare subnet on the opposite ToR and pin a fraction of traffic there. test if spikes reduce. low-risk and reversible.
sara: that sounds good. how do we trigger it?
kevin: I'll push a canary that does 10% route-stitch for tenants matching label "hot-infer". command: ```bash
# create route-stitch canary
redwoodctl infra stitch-egress --region eu-west --selector 'label=hot-infer' --percent 10 --src-tor prefer=backup````
kevin: will also add a probe that samples TCP queue depths on both ToRs every 30s.
maria: and add per-tenant p99 alert with a 5m burn-in to avoid alert storms.
ops-lead: timeline?
kevin: rolling canary in 15m, monitor 30m, if p99 drops proceed to 50% then 100% or keep rolling back consolidation as fallback.
alex: tagging @sara to check it doesn't break SLA tests.
sara: acknowledged. I'll run smoke harness after 10% goes live.
maria: noted — I'll mute noisy paging for the next 45m and watch metrics. :thumbsup: 
ops-lead: assign follow-ups: kevin -> create canary and probes; alex -> correlate tenant maps to ToR; maria -> adjust alerts; sara -> smoke tests. report back in this thread.
kevin: on it, starting deploy in ~10m.
alex: thanks all. we'll avoid a full rollback unless canary fails.
kevin: update 20m later: canary @10% shows p99 reduced by ~60% on affected racks. posting graphs to #dash-links.
maria: nice. keep the canary 30m more then expand.
ops-lead: good first step. let's document egress-path-stitch play in the runbook (infra/egress-playbook) after this.
kevin: will add entry with example command and probe metrics.
sara: smoke passed at 10% canary. no SLA violations observed.
alex: closing loop — will create a postmortem note if we later see recurrence. thanks everyone.
